sections.title: Understanding Visual Intelligence
sections.body: Visual Intelligence, or Machine Intelligence in the context of vision, focuses on how machines perceive and interpret visual information. This involves understanding colors, shapes, and spatial relationships in images, which is crucial for tasks like robotics and computer vision.

sections.title: Color Perception and Curve Recognition
sections.body: One key aspect of visual intelligence is how robots perceive color, which can be represented by averaging RGB values over time. Additionally, recognizing curves such as lines and circles involves using neural networks to extract parameters from these shapes, allowing machines to classify and understand them.

sections.title: Coordinate Transformations
sections.body: To make sense of visual data, we need to convert between different coordinate systems: world coordinates, camera coordinates, and image coordinates. This transformation is essential for accurately mapping what a camera sees to real-world positions, which involves understanding pixel size and image resolution.

sections.title: Distance Measurement and 3D Vision
sections.body: In more advanced applications, binocular vision systems can measure 3D surfaces and calculate distances from points to planes. This requires using specific equations to determine how far a point is from a plane, which is vital for tasks like navigation and object manipulation.

turns.answer: To convert world coordinates to image coordinates
